memo: CASE case_02 — verification notice ('report your qualifying hours'), due 2026-08-05T23:59:00; get_deadline: not breached, 447.0 hours remaining (screening: 19 days remain). GATE 1 (clock): open — proceed. GATE 2 (exemption): screening flags likely exemption 'caretaker_young_child' — member is parent of children ages 6 and 9. Rule: 'A parent, guardian, or caretaker relative of a dependent child age 13 or younger is exempt' (EX-CARETAKER). If confirmed, hours are irrelevant: 'If an exemption applies, the 80-hour requirement does not apply to you at all' (EX-OVERVIEW). Proof per screening and EX-CARETAKER: child's birth certificate or a benefits record showing the child's age. DECISION: likely_exempt. GATE 3 noted for belt-and-suspenders: screening shows 40 qualifying hours/month (40h employment), 40 hours SHORT of the 80-hour standard (REQ-80H); evidence check shows every claimed activity has an accepted document (pay stubs — DOC-WORK: 'Pay stubs covering the month are the cleanest proof'). Plan: submit the exemption claim with the child's birth certificate or benefits record via any Demo State channel (portal, phone, mail form, in person — REQ-DEMOSTATE), and include the 40 hours of pay stubs in the same packet in case the state reads the facts differently. Keep confirmation number/copy. No escalation: deadline open, facts consistent, exemption strongly supported.
member_impact: Good news. You care for children ages 6 and 9. Because they are under 14, the 80-hour work rule likely does not apply to you at all. You do not need to be scared of the 40-hour gap. Here is what to do. Gather one document for each child: a birth certificate, or a benefits record that shows the child's age. Also keep your pay stubs from your cleaning job — send them too, just to be safe. Send everything by August 5, 2026. You can send it online through the member portal, by phone at the state help line, by mail with the form that came with your notice, or in person at the county office. Keep a copy of what you send, and write down any confirmation number. You have time, and you have a clear path. Free help is available at your community organization if you want a hand.

Keep a copy of everything submitted and record the confirmation number
